messages.subject: irace 2.3 with multiple objectives (target-evaluator)
parts:
I have troubles using irace (version 2.3) in a multi-objective setting. In the first irace-iteration everything works perfect. The target runner puts the obtained solution pool in a file for each candidate configuration and each instance, and the target evaluator then uses this information to determine the hypervolume. 

However, in the second iteration something seems to go wrong. The first instance runs smoothly for all candidate configurations. But with the second instance, I can see that the target-runner skips the first two available candidate configurations (the two best/maintained configurations from Iteration 1). However. when calling the target-evaluator, it wants to access the results of these candidate configurations and obviously, irace stops, because target-runner was not run for this instance and candidate configurations.

Could someone help me out with this issue? Am I doing something wrong?

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: irace 2.3 with multiple objectives (target-evaluator)
parts:
Hilde sent me her files and we discovered where the error was. The next version of the user-guide will contain this paragraph to warn users of the potential problem:

If \parameter{targetEvaluator} fails only in the second or later
  iteration, this may because output files or data generated by a previous call
  to \parameter{targetRunner} are missing. Elite configurations are never
  re-executed on the same instance and seed pair, that is, \irace will call
  only once \parameter{targetRunner} for each pair of configuration ID and
  instance ID. However, \parameter{targetEvaluator} is always re-executed,
  which takes into account any updated information (normalization bounds,
  reference sets/points, best-known values, etc.). Thus, any files or data
  generated by \parameter{targetRunner} for a given configuration must remain
  available to \parameter{targetEvaluator} as long as that configuration is
  alive. The list of alive configurations is passed
  to \parameter{targetEvaluator}, which may decide then which data to keep or
  remove.
